name: Fleetwood Mac
hook: A British blues band that recorded with Chicago's blues players in the Chess studio, gave the Beatles the starting point for 'Sun King', and then became, with two Californians, one of the best-selling pop groups in history.
blurb: Fleetwood Mac was started in London in July 1967 by the guitarist Peter Green, who had taken Eric Clapton's place in John Mayall's Bluesbreakers, with Mick Fleetwood and, soon after, John McVie. At first it was a straight British blues band, on Mike Vernon's Blue Horizon label. Their slow, echoing guitar instrumental 'Albatross', released in November 1968, was their only number one in Britain, and George Harrison later said the Beatles started 'Sun King' as an imitation of it. In January 1969, on their American tour, Vernon set up a session in Chicago at the Chess studio, which was about to close, with blues players like Willie Dixon, Otis Spann and Buddy Guy; it came out as 'Fleetwood Mac in Chicago'. Green left in 1970. On New Year's Eve 1974 two Americans, Lindsey Buckingham and Stevie Nicks, joined. In February 1977 the band released 'Rumours', produced by the band with Ken Caillat and Richard Dashut while the couples in the band were breaking up: the McVies divorced, and Buckingham and Nicks split. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year and has sold more than 40 million copies. Christine McVie died in 2022, and in 2024 Nicks said she did not believe the band would continue, though no formal end has been announced.

signatureTracks.title: Albatross
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The blues band at its quietest: a slow instrumental of reverb-soaked guitar that went to number one in Britain and that the Beatles used as a starting point.

signatureTracks.title: Dreams
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: From 'Rumours'. Stevie Nicks's song, built on an almost unchanging bass and drum pattern, and the record most people know the band by.

signatureTracks.title: Go Your Own Way
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Also from 'Rumours': Lindsey Buckingham's song about his split with Nicks, sung with her in the same band.
